title: Certify all-exponent order for general-rank recursive invoices
body:
The common-base Sturm tool cannot compare mixed ranks such as2 and3, and a single power evaluation cannot rule out another crossing. Add a conservative all-exponent certificate for the existing paid-minus-target invoice format. It combines the classical generalized Descartes/Rolle root bound, exact endpoint multiplicity lower bounds and directed rational-power brackets. It certifies uniform order only when every possible root is accounted for; otherwise it returns inconclusive.

For old jobs2,3 and new jobs1,6, the concave-order screen is inconclusive. The new tool proves `(2^t-1)(3^t-1)>0` for every0<t<1. It also finds both interior crossings of `6-4*2^t-3*3^t+2*6^t`, despite equal positive endpoint values. A two-cell grid correctly remains inconclusive. Exact prime valuations certify double endpoint roots without constructing huge powers.

Validation: eight focused tests pass on normal Python3.14.7 and isolated optimized Python3.12.14. They compare610 common-base profiles with the separate exact Sturm classifier and16 mixed-rank factored profiles with integer-power root tests. They cover touching roots, exact grid roots, unresolved signs, outside-domain roots, target debits, cancellation, large coefficients, contract mismatches and real CLI input hashes. The eight existing rational-power tests pass. The new test filename is selected by the current hosted research workflow. `git diff --check` passes. Hosted CI and independent human review are pending.

The tool is deliberately incomplete for general exponential polynomials. A missing certificate is not an equality or an adverse result. It authenticates no construction or supplier and claims no new kappa. Existing frozen sources, selected frontier and five assumptions remain unchanged. [Proof, usage and limits](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/56565b9aec29203bddb14f5d0e76a657d7090699/docs/research/recursive-power-variation.md); [canonical scope](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5784).

Base de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a, priority8. Final public overlap through18:38UTC covered339 open PRs and5165Discussion records; no matching active tool scope was found. Credit the classical theorem, woklerx's specialized T16 crossing proof, mightyOil's moment audit, zxv's invoice interface, the existing directed-power/Sturm tools and their retained predecessors. New integration by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, no subagents. Apache-2.0.
